sources.citation: Currier BS, D'Souza AC, Fiatarone Singh MA, ... Phillips SM. American College of Sports Medicine Position Stand. Resistance Training Prescription for Muscle Function, Hypertrophy, and Physical Performance in Healthy Adults: An Overview of Reviews. Med Sci Sports Exerc 2026;58(4):851-872.
sources.locator: Methods (eligibility), Discussion (effort, volume, progression), Limitations; reference list truncated in capture
sources.findingsUsed: No numeric training-age cutoff; most evidence from novices; training experience had minimal impact on strength and hypertrophy outcomes; sufficient effort by near-failure or a 2-3 RIR target; momentary failure does not enhance gains; insufficient evidence to quantify exact RIR targets; lifting to fatigue inadvisable for some populations (e.g., older); hypertrophy enhanced by about 10 or more weekly sets.
limitations: overview of reviews of mostly untrained participants

sources.citation: American College of Sports Medicine. Position stand: progression models in resistance training for healthy adults. Med Sci Sports Exerc 2009;41(3):687-708.
sources.findingsUsed: Novice: untrained, no RT experience or not trained for several years; intermediate: about 6 months of consistent RT; advanced: years of RT.
limitations: definitions are descriptive, not validated predictors

sources.citation: Videbaek S, Bueno AM, Nielsen RO, Rasmussen S. Incidence of Running-Related Injuries Per 1000 h of running in Different Types of Runners: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis. Sports Med 2015;45(7):1017-1026.
sources.findingsUsed: Injury incidence 17.8 (16.7-19.1) per 1000 h in novice vs 7.7 (6.9-8.7) in recreational runners; no exact definition of runner types; novice cohorts = little or no running experience or not running regularly in the previous 12 months; one recreational cohort required more than 6 accumulated months of regular training; authors suggest a cut-off may be appropriate.
limitations: per-hour incidence is not a dose rule

sources.citation: Refalo MC, Helms ER, Trexler ET, Hamilton DL, Fyfe JJ. Influence of Resistance Training Proximity-to-Failure on Skeletal Muscle Hypertrophy: A Systematic Review with Meta-analysis. Sports Med 2023;53(3):649-665.
sources.locator: Abstract (Results, Conclusion), Results (search), Discussion (practical application, limitations)
sources.findingsUsed: Set failure vs non-failure ES 0.19 (0.00-0.37), trivial; momentary failure vs non-failure ES 0.12 (-0.13 to 0.37); a majority of sets with close proximity to failure recommended; possible non-linear relation; only two set-failure studies in resistance-trained participants.
limitations: a published letter disputes some cited references

sources.citation: Robinson ZP, Pelland JC, Remmert JF, Refalo MC, Jukic I, Steele J, Zourdos MC. Exploring the dose-response relationship between estimated resistance training proximity to failure, strength gain, and muscle hypertrophy: a series of meta-regressions. Sports Med 2024;54(9):2209-2231.
sources.findingsUsed: Strength gains similar across a wide RIR range; hypertrophy improves as sets end closer to failure; exploratory; exact relation unclear given RIR estimation.

sources.citation: Schwellnus M, Adami PE, Bougault V, et al. International Olympic Committee (IOC) consensus statement on acute respiratory illness in athletes part 1: acute respiratory infections. Br J Sports Med 2022;56(19):1066-1088.
sources.access: FULL_TEXT (accepted postprint, decoded locally; not the typeset version)
sources.findingsUsed: RTS is a continuum whose rate depends on severity, complications and normal responses to progressive load; most ARill are mild and short and ~20% cost more than one training day; mild ARinf is self-managed with a daily pre-exercise checklist (fever, chills, excessive fatigue, general muscle aches, breathing difficulty, chest pain/pressure/tightness, dizziness or palpitations at rest, moderate-severe cough, severe headache, persistent/severe nose-throat symptoms, persistent abdominal symptoms, not feeling well enough; plus chronic-condition risk factors); then a self-administered challenge at 60-70% of normal intensity, 10-20 min, stopped and referred on listed symptoms during, after and 24 h after exercise (incl. very dark urine); moderate or severe ARinf under professional care.
limitations: decoded text, page numbers of the postprint

sources.citation: Frandsen JSB, Hulme A, Parner ET, ... Nielsen RO. How much running is too much? Identifying high-risk running sessions in a 5200-person cohort study. Br J Sports Med 2025;59(17):1203-1210.
sources.findingsUsed: Reference = longest distance run in the past 30 days (device data); single-session spikes >10% associated with overuse injury (HRR 1.64, 1.52, 2.28 by spike size); ACWR negative dose-response; week-to-week ratio no relationship.
limitations: whether races were in the reference not verified

sources.citation: Spiering BA, Mujika I, Sharp MA, Foulis SA. Maintaining Physical Performance: The Minimal Dose of Exercise Needed to Preserve Endurance and Strength Over Time. J Strength Cond Res 2021;35(5):1449-1458.
sources.findingsUsed: Endurance maintained up to 15 weeks with volume reduced 33-66% if intensity is kept; strength and size (younger) up to 32 weeks with 1 session/week, 1 set/exercise; intensity is the key variable; insufficient data for athletes.

sources.citation: Chamorro-Vina C, Fernandez-del-Valle M, Tacon AM. Excessive Exercise and Immunity: The J-Shaped Curve. In: The Active Female (Springer, 2013/2014), ch. 24, pp. 357-372.

returnLadder.transitionRule: A rung is left only after a whole plan week of the affected sport at that rung was executed (the BR-Q4 completion test for that sport: every session executed, no adverse or conflicting response) and the warning signs were re-answered no at that week's review. Otherwise the rung repeats: missed or partial repeats it with no debt; one adverse response repeats it and asks the exercise-response items; the existing repeated-adverse regression applies; any warning sign yes routes S3. Strength sets come back at most one set per executed week whatever the rung (the D49 rule). Never by date alone; the speed choice is never evidence (RC-12).
returnLadder.loadReference: Loads logged on R2/R3 rows (chosen by effort below the current load) never replace the held reference load downward or upward; they are tolerance evidence only. At R4 the held reference returns and the existing gates judge it.

items.question: A1 (a)-(c): reason-screen semantics
designRows: Block 1 A1 (a) ask only what is missing
A1 (c) body words that are not about the body

confidence.rationale: The screen stays fail-closed: free text alone never yields NONCLINICAL, and every ambiguity or third-party mention ends in one explicit structured question with its own exit. The residual is the same self-report residual the eligibility screen already carries. Lexicon coverage in PT-BR/EN/ES is not exhaustive and was not tested by this instance.

items.approvedRule: (a) No category: ask interruption.reasonCategory. A structured nonclinical category with free text that is ambiguous or names someone else's condition: ask once interruption.clinicalReason (yes/no): 'Did this break involve your own pain, injury, illness, pregnancy or recent childbirth, or another medical reason?' (PT-BR/EN/ES). An explicit no (isNo) with a structured nonclinical category resolves only the AMBIGUOUS_REASON basis (ambiguous words and phrases, body words, locally negated damage) and the third-party basis to NONCLINICAL. It never resolves a clinical category, a clinical flag, a self-attributed clinical word, phrase or damage-plus-body mention, a mid-clause or conditioned denial (a contradiction between text and answer is ASK, PCG O01/RC-05), CONTRADICTORY_FLAGS, INVALID_CLINICAL_FLAG, or a missing or unrecognized category; current eligibility flags still apply; yes stays CLINICAL (R-F08-1). (b) A clause that names another person by a possessive or article plus a noun from a closed, versioned list (family member, partner, child, friend, pet) and holds no first-person marker: its clinical words, phrases and damage mentions are a third-party mention, asked as in (a), never the athlete's clinical mention and never NONCLINICAL by text. First-person markers: I, me, myself, my/mine with a body part, we, us, our(s); eu, me, comigo, nos, a gente, meu/minha with a body part, nosso/nossa; yo, me, mi, conmigo, nosotros/nosotras, mi with a body part, nuestro/nuestra; and first-person forms of clinical verbs. A clause mixing both stays clinical; the clause split is unchanged. (c) 'back' in the listed adverbial collocations (back from, came/got/went/flew/drove back, back home, back to, be back) is not a body word, for the matched token only; 'back' after a possessive, article or modifier (my/the/lower/upper back) stays a body word. 'on my/our/his/her feet' is not a body mention. No such exception applies in a clause holding a damage verb or a clinical word or phrase; other ambiguous words in the clause still ask. 'baby' and the maternity, newborn and breastfeeding words stay ambiguous and are asked once with the pregnancy and childbirth wording. (d) Everything listed in DESIGN A1 (d) is unchanged.
items.modification: Relative to the DESIGN: (1) the confirmation names pregnancy and recent childbirth, because PREGNANCY and POSTPARTUM are clinical categories and the V1 population excludes them (I01 population line); (2) first-person plural markers count as first person; (3) idiom and adverb exceptions never apply in a clause with a damage verb or a clinical word; possessive/article/modifier + 'back' stays a body word; (4) a structured no never resolves a conditioned or mid-clause denial; (5) R-F08-1 is protected across the screen change (condition C-Q01-5).
conditions: C-Q01-1: The clinicalReason answer is part of that report's facts (append-only, in its inputHash), asked once per report, starts unanswered and is actively answered (SEC-V1CP-03); unknown is ASK.

C-Q01-2: The third-party noun list, the first-person markers and the adverb collocations are closed, versioned lexicon data in all three V1 languages; PT 'em pe' and ES 'de pie' may be added under the same rules (recommended for parity; without them those texts stay ASK).
C-Q01-3: Free text can still only add CLINICAL or ASK; no text alone ever yields NONCLINICAL (operational.return.reasonScreen).

C-Q01-4: Directed tests: the four holdout texts (H07 becomes ASK then NONCLINICAL only on a structured no); 'my son had the flu, I caught it' CLINICAL; 'my wife and I had covid' and 'we all got sick' CLINICAL; 'visiting my dad in hospital' ASK; 'got back pain', 'back from hospital' CLINICAL; 'my back was killing me' ASK; 'cut on my feet' clinical (damage plus body); 'didn't feel any pain until I ran' with clinicalReason no stays ASK; 'new baby' asked with the childbirth wording; every case in the three languages.

C-Q01-5: A report the runtime classed CLINICAL under an earlier screen version stays a clinical-cause episode. Before launch, Engineering confirms no persisted athlete record predates the change; once records persist, the first-recorded screen outcome is kept per report and R-F08-1 reads the stricter of the recorded and the current outcome (routed to PCG and Engineering).
C-Q01-6: Copy is G03/Product-UX; it never says the athlete is 'cleared' and never implies the coach ruled out illness.

items.question: E1: training-age mapping per sport
designRows: Block 1 E data-path audit (Founder synthetic athlete)

confidence.rationale: The boundary values rest on descriptive, heterogeneous definitions (strength: a 2009 consensus abstract; running: no standard, one cohort's >6-month criterion). Harm is bounded because the derived category never sets capacity and the existing establishment rules still apply; misclassification mainly changes the walk/jog vs 20-minute easy entry and exercise skill admissibility.

items.approvedRule: Per sport, an optional intake field trainingMonths (months of regular training, most weeks, in the current continuous period ending now) is read only when that sport's category is absent: 0 = NONE; 1-5 = NOVICE; 6-23 = INTERMEDIATE; 24 or more = EXPERIENCED. An explicit category always wins. The derived category never sets current capacity: weekly minutes, days, longest run and loads stay their own facts and unknown stays unknown. A stop of longPauseWeeksAtLeast (4) weeks or more ends a period and is the existing pause fact (RESTART). A value that is not a whole number from 0 up to the athlete's age in months is asked.
conditions: C-Q03-1: The question defines 'regular' and 'current continuous period', per sport, in the three languages; a lifetime total is never used (an earlier period before a long stop is history: ACSM 2009 counts 'not trained for several years' as novice).
C-Q03-2: EXPERIENCED derived at 24 months is a label with no dose effect today (the runtime treats INTERMEDIATE and EXPERIENCED alike); any rule that distinguishes them re-opens this boundary.
C-Q03-3: The derived category is recorded with basis DERIVED_FROM_TRAINING_MONTHS and disclosed in the cold-start explanation.
C-Q03-4: Strength skill admissibility for a derived INTERMEDIATE still passes the existing establishment rules (effort-guided from the lightest load, technique first, SKILL_MISMATCH step back).

C-Q03-5: E1 never replaces current exposure: for the Founder athlete (10 months) the result is INTERMEDIATE in both sports, run EASY_UNKNOWN (20-minute easy entry) while weekly minutes are unknown, strength FAMILIAR_UNKNOWN_LOAD; the smallest missing input remains current weekly running minutes and days (G03/Product: ask them).
C-Q03-6: trainingMonths is a new intake field: Security/G07 confirm it (it is not health data, but it is profiling data).

newParameters.name: trainingMonths bands (both sports)
newParameters.basis: Strength: S02 (ABSTRACT_ONLY) intermediate about 6 months of consistent RT, advanced years; S01 (FULL_TEXT) no cutoff, experience had minimal impact on outcomes, most evidence in novices. Running: S03 (FULL_TEXT) novice cohorts = little or no experience or not running regularly in the previous 12 months, one recreational cohort = more than 6 accumulated months of regular training, no established cutoff.

items.question: E2: race results, or history only
items.decisiveBasis: Internal: the approved single-run ceiling definition (I01: longest completed run in the window; intake ceiling in the first cold-start week) applied to a fact type it already covers (a completed run), with the probe confirming the effect. No new dose or number; S07 is context only.

confidence.rationale: A completed race is a completed run session, which is what the approved single-run ceiling reads; the probe shows the effect is a week-1 redistribution inside availability. Whether the cohort behind the ceiling counted races was not verified (abstract only).

items.approvedRule: A race result with distance, duration and date counts as one completed run session of that duration (time on feet, not a claim of continuous running) only when recent.longestRunMinutes is not reported, the result is dated within the intake's existing 28-day window and not after the intake date, and the athlete confirms it was completed and tolerated (the existing currentFamiliar confirmations). It is then used exactly as a reported longest run for the week-1 long-run cap and as the single-run ceiling reference (INTAKE_REPORTED_LONGEST). It never enters the below-minimum walk/jog test, the run class, weekly minutes or days, pace, effort zone, intensity, quality familiarity, the event or race-day statement, or a prediction. Older or undated results are history (records) only.
items.modification: Relative to the DESIGN: 'continuous' is removed (a race may include walking); 'classification' is removed (a race value under run.minimumSessionMinutes would flip an intermediate runner to walk/jog, see probe); the tolerated confirmation is required.
conditions: C-Q04-1: Directed tests from the probe: 120 min / 3 days with and without a race (class unchanged, week 1 within availability); a sub-15-minute race never makes WALK_JOG; a NOVICE EASY_LOW class unchanged; a race older than 28 days changes nothing.
C-Q04-2: The tolerated question is a structured answer (Security/G07); a pain or injury answer goes to the existing eligibility screen.
C-Q04-3: The explanation states the race was read as 'a recent run of about N minutes', never as a fitness estimate.

items.question: F08 Situation 1: the intent table

confidence.rationale: The consensus content is for acute respiratory infections; 'mild illness' in V1 also covers other mild illnesses (e.g., gastrointestinal), so part of it is extrapolated. The intents use existing doses; the instrument is pending G04 revalidation and Security's vocabulary confirmation.

items.authorityCondition: Valid only if PCG-V1CP-F08 r2 (DR-148 clauses 2, 5 and 6, the G04-row delta, Q4 and RC-01..RC-18) passes its narrow fidelity re-check and the Chief consolidates it as written. Until then Situation 1 is not implementable and F08 stays F08_OPEN. The MILD_ILLNESS path also rests on DR-148's partial supersession of DR-99 and of SSCTR-05's 'suspected illness' for this subset (read under DR-148; the constitution text is unchanged, and the PCG-proposed pointer is the Chief's to apply).
items.approvedRule: Intents map to rungs (returnLadder): REST R0; LIGHT_ACTIVITY_ONLY R1; REDUCE_SUBSTANTIAL R2; REDUCE_LIGHT R3, which reduces difficulty first (no hard work in running; every strength set at 4 or more reps in reserve) with a light volume cut (consolidation long run, consolidation set count). Intents offered: MILD_ILLNESS and MILD_INDISPOSITION: R2, R1 or R0 (no long run and no near-normal strength volume while unwell); UNUSUAL_FATIGUE, MINOR_DISCOMFORT and NEED_REST: R3, R2, R1 or R0. Affected sports: systemic conditions (MILD_ILLNESS, MILD_INDISPOSITION, UNUSUAL_FATIGUE) always affect both programmed sports; for local conditions the affected sports are the athlete's explicit per-sport statement, never inferred (RC-13), both when unstated; an UPPER_BODY or LOWER_BODY statement limits the strength intent to that region's rows. Any week holding window days of an affected sport HOLDs that sport's gates (no step from a reduced week). Entry needs every warning sign (warningSignInstrument) actively answered no and no current clinical sign (RC-03).
items.modification: Relative to the DESIGN: (1) REDUCE_LIGHT is no longer the CONSOLIDATION dose, which holds intensity and keeps quality sessions: it becomes R3 (exact operation in returnLadder.rungs[R3]); (2) REDUCE_LIGHT is not offered for MILD_ILLNESS or MILD_INDISPOSITION; (3) scopes follow the athlete's per-sport statement (RC-13); (4) a stricter warning-sign instrument (FP-1); (5) explicit window-end, chaining and race rules below.
conditions: C-Q05-1 (window end): the return starts only after the athlete's structured answers that every warning sign is no and the condition has resolved or clearly improved; not improved follows warningSignInstrument.persistence (no new window).

C-Q05-2 (chaining, RC-06): no new Situation 1 window for a systemic condition, or for a local condition in the same or an overlapping scope, until the previous window's return ladder has completed (R5 reached after a whole executed plan week at R4 with no adverse response). A report before that is not re-windowed: it is screened (warning signs; persistentPain for discomfort; the scoped illness question, Q4 b); any yes routes S3; all no holds the ladder's current rung that week; the same condition reported again at the next weekly review leads to the professional-assessment recommendation and S3. A continuous Situation 1 window never exceeds 14 days.

C-Q05-3 (race in a window): agreed with the DESIGN handler. A window holding the race day asks about the race (keep the date and end the window before it, move it, or skip it); the race is never silently kept or dropped. Inside an R0-R3 window no race-effort touch or quality session is prescribed. For a systemic-condition window the question says the coach does not plan a race while the athlete is unwell (copy G03, wording pending G04).

C-Q05-4 (re-ask, RF-7): warning signs at entry, at each weekly review inside the window and the ladder, at the window end, and with any session reported ADVERSE or CONFLICTING there (then the exercise-response items).
C-Q05-5: A REDUCE window whose sessions were not executed is read as a rest window of its days for the return.
C-Q05-6: The window stays a Situation 1 fact (RC-07); it is never converted into a declared break, and a declared break is never converted into it.
C-Q05-7: Clinical first (RC-01); free text is not an F08 input (SEC-V1CP-05); unknown is ASK (RF-2); all-no is never shown as safe (RF-4).
C-Q05-8: Security confirms the added booleans and the improvement question before any real collection (SEC-V1CP-02, RC-17).

C-Q05-9: Directed tests: each condition x intent pair allowed or refused as above; each warning sign yes routes S3 for every sport; an unanswered sign is ASK; the race-in-window question; chaining refused with S3 on persistence; regional scope applied only to the stated region; the unaffected sport unchanged.

items.question: F08 return speeds

confidence.rationale: Moderate for the direction (gradual, evidence-conditioned, no rest-to-full jump); low for the exact number of rungs and holds, which no evidence quantifies: they only hold doses already tolerated.

items.approvedRule: Speeds are rung sequences on returnLadder; each rung lasts one executed week (transitionRule). Window REDUCE_LIGHT: FASTER R4 then R5; BALANCED R3, R4, R5; CONSERVATIVE R3, R4, R4, R5. Window REDUCE_SUBSTANTIAL: FASTER R3, R4, R5; BALANCED R2, R3, R4, R5; CONSERVATIVE R2, R3, R4, R4, R5. Window REST or LIGHT_ACTIVITY_ONLY of 10 days or less: FASTER R3, R4, R5; BALANCED R2, R3, R4, R5; CONSERVATIVE the MODERATE recipe (entry dose, then moderateStepsToPrior conditional steps, prior doses the ceiling), then R5. Window REST or LIGHT_ACTIVITY_ONLY of 11-14 days: FASTER the MODERATE recipe; BALANCED the MODERATE recipe with its first step held one more executed week; CONSERVATIVE the MODERATE recipe with each step held one more executed week. No window of 14 days or less is ever read as LONG (no restart, no clearing of achieved history). Default BALANCED; the speed can change until the window ends; it is never itself evidence (RC-12, B2); the speeds end at R5, never multiply with the coach profiles (profile gates act inside them only as holds) and never pass a cap.
items.modification: Relative to the DESIGN: (1) no speed goes from a rest or a substantial reduction straight to the pre-window doses: FASTER after rest or REDUCE_SUBSTANTIAL climbs through R3 (RC-12: gradual at every speed); (2) BALANCED is a climb, not 'the class recipe plus one hold', so the first week back has no hard work; (3) CONSERVATIVE never reads a window as LONG; (4) the D49 one-set-per-week rule applies to strength on every rung; (5) the window's logs never replace the held reference load.
items.fp4Note: The only step from a reduced rung to the held pre-window dose is FASTER after a REDUCE_LIGHT window (R3 executed during the window, then R4). It mirrors the existing consolidation-to-development transition and is conditioned on the window's executed weeks. If the Founder reads 'gradual' more strictly, FASTER after REDUCE_LIGHT becomes R3, R4, R5 and equals BALANCED for that window. Founder question (FP-4), non-blocking.
conditions: C-Q06-1: Every rung transition follows returnLadder.transitionRule; an adverse response repeats the rung, a warning sign routes S3.
C-Q06-2: After any window the first quality slot runs easy (R4).

C-Q06-3: Directed tests: each window x speed sequence; no sequence reaches the pre-window dose before an executed R3 or MODERATE step (except FP-4's case); an 11-14 day CONSERVATIVE never restarts or clears history; strength sets never rise more than one per executed week; a missed rung repeats; the speed change before and after the window end.
C-Q06-4: Copy explains each speed concretely (for example 'one easy week, then your usual plan') and never presents a speed as clearance; speeds are not the coach profiles (D2.2).

newParameters.name: return-speed rung sequences and hold units
newParameters.value: as approvedRule (one executed week per rung; BALANCED and CONSERVATIVE add holds of one executed week)
newParameters.basis: RC-12; S06 (graded RTS, progression on normal responses, first exposure at moderate intensity); S08 abstract (reduced training for 14 days or less maintains most capacity, so the ladder is a tolerance check); existing recipes (I01)
newParameters.population: V1 nonclinical adults returning from a Situation 1 window

items.reReviewTrigger: The Founder's FP-4 answer; any change to RC-12 or the return recipes; product data on returns after windows; a new consensus on graded return after illness.

items.question: F08 Situation 2: per-sport entry and triggers, conditional on the PCG form

confidence.rationale: Moderate for the dose mechanics, which reuse existing recipes with a conservative floor. Whether a person may train after a relevant illness or injury is not assessed here: that part is OUT_OF_SCOPE_CLINICAL and stays with the person and their professional.

items.authorityCondition: Valid only if DR-148 clauses 3, 5 and 6 and the G04-row delta, with P-2-r2, C01-r2, C02-r2 and RC-08..RC-10, RC-12, RC-13 and RC-15, are consolidated as written. The restart is a sporting restart after the person's declaration, never a clearance (RC-02). This record approves no clinical return or clearance and assesses no person (SSCTR-05).
items.approvedRule: Per sport declared ready: the return class from the episode's own days, counted from its first day to that sport's declaration date (per sport, forward only: PCG O02), never below MODERATE (no SHORT resume after a clinical hold); no current-demonstration entry; the existing recipes (returnEntry, returnStrength, strengthEntryWeek, D49). Options: BALANCED (default) = the class recipe with its first step held one more executed week; CONSERVATIVE = the next class's recipe (MODERATE to LONG; LONG stays LONG). No FASTER. Restrictions from the closed vocabulary are hard caps above profile, volume, difficulty and speed: AVOID_LOWER_BODY_STRENGTH removes lower-region strength rows and AVOID_UPPER_BODY_STRENGTH upper-region rows, never replaced by another exercise or by a load from another exercise; when a restriction ends by the person's later structured statement, that region restarts by its own return recipe (entry dose, D49), never at prior loads (RC-09). A sport declared not ready stays held and the other proceeds with the existing composition (RC-13). Back to S3 on any warning sign (warningSignInstrument, entry and exercise-response items), an eligibility flag, a clinical reason or mention, pain with a substitution, or symptoms reported back; a new declaration dated after it is then required (RC-10). S6 ends by the existing return completion (executed evidence).
items.modification: Relative to the DESIGN: (1) MODERATE is the minimum class after a clinical hold, so a short episode never resumes at last doses; (2) an ADVERSE or CONFLICTING session response during the restart is asked against the warning-sign items and never only held (the Phase 3.4 Q8 condition carried); (3) running restarts with AVOID_LOWER_BODY_STRENGTH only if the declaration answers an explicit item that running itself is not restricted (Q4 f: the software infers nothing); AVOID_UPPER_BODY_STRENGTH does not hold running, which is declared on its own; (4) per-sport dating (O02).
conditions: C-Q07-1: No clearance wording, field or label anywhere (RC-02); copy 'you told us you are ready to return', never 'cleared' (G8).

C-Q07-2: The declaration is append-only, bound to this athlete's clinical hold on record, every item actively answered, never a single checkbox (RC-08); it never edits or reclassifies the episode (R-F08-1).
C-Q07-3: S6 is computed by the runtime from the declaration fact (RC-15), never by a client dropping the continuation state (C07).

C-Q07-4: Directed tests: no declaration stays clinical; a declaration with any warning sign stays clinical; a clean declaration restarts at MODERATE or above, without old loads; restrictions respected and never substituted; RUN with AVOID_LOWER without the explicit item stays held; one sport held and the other active; a recurrent symptom and an adverse response route back with an ASK; a reason change still has no exit; history preserved; no option passes a cap.

items.decisiveBasis: Internal: the existing cold start and RESTART rules (I01, I02) and the PCG form (I06); the added condition only removes an inconsistency between two existing rules (I04 O04). No new physiological claim.

confidence.rationale: Existing cold-start and RESTART rules; the added condition only removes an existing inconsistency (O04) for this path.

items.authorityCondition: After a long nonclinical interruption: existing authority. After a clinical hold: DR-148 clause 4 and RC-11 as consolidated, and only with a valid readiness declaration.
items.approvedRule: The new program comes from the existing cold start (generateProgram) on an updated intake plus the carried record. Per sport the pause is computed from the record (weeks since that sport's last executed session) and the existing RESTART rules apply (run restart at longPauseWeeksAtLeast or more; strength known doses ignored on a long pause). Prior history, records and achieved peaks are context (priorCapacity), never dose and never shown as current capacity.
conditions: C-Q08-1: The record bounds the updated intake's recent exposure: recent weekly minutes and days never exceed what the record shows executed in the period it covers; unknown stays unknown.

C-Q08-2 (coherence, O04): the new plan never starts a sport above the start the in-program return of the same record pause would set (SHORT or MODERATE recipe), and after a clinical hold never above the S6 restart for that sport (MODERATE floor, restrictions in force, not-ready sports held).
C-Q08-3: Restrictions in force carry over (RC-11); any current sign still routes clinical; the intake reads the declaration instead of re-routing the historic episode.
C-Q08-4: Race results older than 28 days are history only (Q04).

C-Q08-5: Directed tests: a 3-week nonclinical pause never starts above the MODERATE entry; a post-hold plan with AVOID_LOWER keeps the restriction; a not-ready sport is not programmed; history unchanged.

confidence.rationale: P1, P2 and P4 only hold or advise inside the reviewed envelope; P5 is rejected for lack of applicable evidence.

CONSERVATIVE: a completed run with no reported response (COMPLETED_NO_RESPONSE) holds its run gate in EASY-mode development weeks; never REGRESS, never adverse; not applied in WALK_JOG, RESTART or RETURN modes (return recipes unchanged).
conditions: The output says the step waits for a reported effort and recovery.

items.question: Difficulty levers D1 (LOWER and the HIGHER new parameter), D2 and D3
designRows: Blocks 3-4 axes table: D1, D2, D3

leverDecisions.rule: The FROM_LOG instruction threshold is startRir (3), and a development step (and an above-plan load adoption) needs the logged minimum RIR at or above the prescribed RIR (tolerance 0; P3's content). The regression bound stays prescribed minus one: a log one RIR short holds and never regresses. Establishment, re-establishment, unlogged, return-entry, return-step and event-phase rows are unchanged.

HYPERTROPHY accessory loaded rows (KNOWN or FROM_LOG; never MAIN, PRACTICE, bodyweight, band or assisted rows) are prescribed at RIR 2 (targetRir) with the instruction 'add reps while at least 1 in reserve' (acceptance prescribed minus one = 1, tolerance unchanged). GENERAL accessory loaded rows: instruction threshold 2 (targetRir - 1, inside today's acceptance; prescribed RIR stays 3).
conditions: Strength experience INTERMEDIATE or EXPERIENCED, declared or derived (Q03).

Development phases only (BUILD, DEVELOPMENT, NEXT_BLOCK, CONSOLIDATION); never ESTABLISHMENT, RESTART, RETURN entry or steps, re-establishment, SPECIFIC, TAPER, RACE_WEEK or POST_EVENT, nor inside a Situation 1 window, its ladder or an S6 restart.

items.approvedRule: 1. One axis per lever, holding with Q09-Q11: the RIR threshold and the step tolerance are Difficulty's; the easy-run duration step is Volume's (LOWER only); EARNED never releases an easy-duration step that LOWER volume withholds. 2. The envelope comes last and is the same for every choice: clinical screen and clinical-first, R-F08-1, the F08 instrument and S3 routes, eligibility, single-run ceiling, long-run share, availability, event phase doses and proximity rules, return classes and recipes (D49, strengthEntryWeek), establishment and cold-start rules, the gates' HOLD and REGRESS on missed, partial, adverse or conflicting evidence, the systemic hold, the Situation 1 ladder and the S6 options. 3. The profile never overrides a volume or difficulty choice (now true by construction). 4. HIGHER difficulty is never a bypass: D1 HIGHER only within Q11's conditions; D2 HIGHER only changes the default presentation of an optional element today's plan offers; D3 HIGHER only selects the upper bound of the approved taper range; no HIGHER choice changes any gate, cap, ceiling, phase minimum RIR, return recipe, F08 rule or the clinical screen. 5. HIGHER volume never exceeds the chosen days and minutes; where it equals STANDARD the output says so. 6. A change of choice is a PREFERENCE_CHANGE recorded as a decision that re-plans only weeks after this one from the current state; executed history and this week's sessions are unchanged; in the last week it is KEEP, recorded for the next program; the same choice again changes nothing.

aeReview.answer: Current plan adequate? FREEZE-6 behaviour stays the default byte for byte; the deltas add athlete choices and legitimate exits, they replace no adequate default.
Material facts with provenance? Every lever reads structured, append-only facts (choices, Situation 1 reports, declarations, the record); free text never opens anything.
KEEP defensible? Yes for the default path and the last week (KEEP); not for H07 (no exit), H28 (an inconsistent strength restart) or F08 (no legitimate return, B6).

Change necessary? A1, A3, E1 and E2 fix documented defects (holdout O01, O02, the data-path audit); F08 is required before launch (D2.5, B6); profiles, volume and difficulty are Founder-mandated capabilities (D1.4).
Smallest sufficient intervention? Existing doses, recipes and range bounds wherever possible; new values only E1's bands and D1 HIGHER's RIR; holds counted in executed weeks.

Why smaller options fail? Resending the break was A1's only exit and none existed for H07; option B keeps a SUBOPTIMAL restart; the DESIGN's consolidation REDUCE_LIGHT keeps hard sessions and so does not reduce difficulty; one-step FASTER rows were not gradual (RC-12).
Priority and progression protected? Key runs are protected (no hard work in ladders, D1 HIGHER upper-body only for runners); every restoration needs executed evidence; no ladder skips a rung.
Evidence supports conclusion and dose? Per item; P5 rejected and lower-body D1 HIGHER for runners abstained for lack of evidence.

Material uncertainty: E1's exact boundaries; any benefit of RIR 1; extrapolation from respiratory infection to other mild illnesses; the number of rungs and holds; warning-sign content (G04); the reliability of self-report.
ASK, HOLD or CLINICAL_HUMAN_REQUIRED needed? Yes: A1 asks once; F08 warning signs, persistence and S6 triggers route the clinical hold; unknown is ASK; clinical judgment stays outside the software.
